description: The owner question flow: closed questions whose answers build an FXI and an FXE. Questions are asked in this order, each only when its `when` condition holds. Options carry the code they write in `value`; `usual` keeps the published default; `unknown` writes `?`.

facts.exercise: The subject is an exercise (the usual answer to "subject").
facts.equipment: The subject is a piece of equipment on its own.
facts.template: The movement is one of the published movement words.
facts.motion-from-scratch: The movement is "other", or the owner said the joint movement differs from the movement word.
facts.posture-has-usual: The movement word fixes a posture.
facts.load-has-usual: The movement word fixes the load (body weight, a cable, a machine, a named implement).
facts.load-holdable: The first load is a free implement, a cable, a Smith machine or a landmine.
facts.hold-has-usual: The rules give a usual hold point for that implement in this movement.
facts.load-band: A band is one of the loads.
facts.load-machine: The load is a strength machine.
facts.load-cardio: The load is a cardio machine.
facts.machine-has-usual: The movement word fixes which machine is used.
facts.cardio-has-usual: The movement word fixes which cardio machine is used.
facts.hold2-has-usual: The rules give a usual hold point for the second implement in this movement.
facts.machine-direction-has-usual: The movement word names a multi-joint machine, so its direction is known.
facts.contact-has-usual: The movement word names the machine, or the rules give a default contact for the guided motion.
facts.eq-contact-has-usual: The rules give a default contact for the guided motion of the equipment.
facts.eq2-contact-has-usual: The rules give a default contact for the guided motion of the second setup.
facts.single-phase-template: The movement word has one phase with joint actions, so its kind can change on its own.
facts.stance-recorded: The body position at the start is standing, standing bent over, either or unknown; or the feet push a machine's foot plate (leg press).
facts.word-asks: The chosen movement word carries closed questions of its own in the movement-word dataset.

questions.text: Are you describing an exercise, or a piece of equipment on its own?
questions.help: An exercise gets an FXI and the FXE of its main equipment. Equipment on its own gets a registry FXE.
questions.usual: An exercise.

options.label: A piece of equipment on its own

questions.layer: FXI m, and the defaults of every other layer
questions.text: Which movement is it?
questions.help: Pick the movement word that matches the exercise as you would name it with nothing added. Variations come next. Pick "other" only when no word fits. The movement words themselves are not part of the notation: the encoder loads them from a movement-word dataset.

options.label: Something else: describe the joint movement step by step
I do not know how it is done

questions.layer: FXI layers the movement word fixes
questions.text: The movement word's own closed questions, if it has any.
questions.help: Some movement words carry one or two closed questions of their own (is the knee straight or bent; which limbs lift). Each option patches the layers the word fixes. The questions, their options and their patches come with the movement-word dataset.
questions.usual: The option the movement word means when nothing else is said, where the dataset gives one.

questions.layer: selects which layers differ from their defaults
questions.text: What, if anything, is different from the usual way of doing this movement?
questions.help: The usual way is what the movement word means with nothing added: "squat" is both feet, no held posture, full range. Pick every way your exercise, as you actually run it, differs, whether or not its name says so. Each pick opens one question. For "other" or "unknown" movements, body position, equipment and sides are asked anyway.
questions.importHelp: Import mode: body differences (motion, position, footwork, support, equipment) may come from the description; sides, grip, stance, range, held posture and line of pull come only from the name, the alternate name and the fields (the source rule).
questions.usual: Nothing differs.

The kind of motion: explosive with flight, continuous, a hold, a static or dynamic stretch
The body position (standing, seated, lying, kneeling, hanging)
The rep ends in a different body position from its start (get-up)

What the body rests on, beyond the floor
The equipment that loads the muscles
How the sides work: one side then the other, alternating, reciprocal

Range: partial, deeper than usual, or from a deficit
Where each rep starts: the floor, the hang, pins or blocks
A held posture of limbs that do not work: hands behind the head, arms crossed, free leg forward
The line of pull: cable or band anchored high or low, from the side, or the load passing behind the head
An accessory that helps without loading: a strap, towel or rope pulling a limb, or a partner

questions.text: How many separate movements does one rep have?
questions.help: Ask one closed question for each pair of movements: does the second start before the first ends? Yes: one phase (a thruster: the press starts while you still rise). No: two phases (squat, stand, then press; a push-up then a shoulder-blade push). Never count the lowering or return.
questions.importHelp: Import mode, text silent: two movement words in one name are two phases in name order, unless the name is a one-phase word (thruster).

questions.text: What kind of movement is phase 1?
questions.help: Pick how the joints move. "Explosive" or "fast" alone is a normal rep: ballistic needs flight or release. A slam is ballistic even when the implement stays in the hands (a battle rope slam).
questions.usual: A normal moving rep.

questions.text: Which joints move in phase 1?
questions.help: Count a joint only when the working muscles move it through a clear range (about 30° or more) as part of what the exercise trains. Never count a joint held still on purpose: the knee in a Romanian deadlift or hip thrust, the elbow in a fly or lateral raise, the spine unless bending or twisting the trunk is the exercise, the ankle unless the exercise rises onto the toes or pushes off.

questions.text: What is the body position at the start of the rep?
questions.help: Flat means within about 15° of horizontal; incline and decline 15–60°. Hinged forward and held there (bent-over row) is "standing, bent". On hands and knees, in a plank or a push-up is "prone". The trunk decides: kneeling with the trunk folded forward over the thighs (child's pose) is "prone"; "kneeling" has the trunk upright. On a machine, use your body position.
questions.usual: The position the movement word fixes.

options.label: The usual position for this movement
options.whenNot: no movement word with a fixed position was chosen

Held up by the hands or arms, feet off the floor: hanging from a bar, propped on dip bars.
Upside down, trunk within 30° of vertical, head lowest: handstand, headstand.

questions.text: Where is it held?
questions.help: In the hands, at the sides, swung or by a handle is "hands", and so are dumbbells held at shoulder height and a bar pressed without resting on the shoulders. Resting on the front of the shoulders (front rack), or a landmine end held at the shoulder, is "shoulders". A bar behind the neck rests on the "back". Straight-armed overhead for the whole rep is "overhead". A load on the lap in a seated calf raise is "thighs". A band goes where it presses or pulls on the body; in leg-only work that is usually the feet or ankles. A band whose ends you hold at the shoulders (a band thruster) is "hands": "shoulders" is a load resting on them.

questions.text: How do the two sides work?
questions.help: Doing every rep on one side and then switching is different from alternating sides rep by rep. Reciprocal means both sides move at once in opposite directions: walking, flutter kicks, alternating rope waves. A stretch or roll that works one limb and then the other is "one side, then the other". Legs that pedal are reciprocal even when the trunk turns to each side in turn (bicycle crunch); a trunk turn alone has no sides.
questions.importHelp: Import mode: from the name and fields only. "Alternating" means the sides take turns only when nothing else in the name alternates ("alternating front and lateral raise" alternates two raises).
questions.usual: What the movement word says, else both sides together.

questions.text: Where does the load pull from, compared with the usual way?
questions.help: Usual anchors: low for curls, raises, upright rows, shrugs, kickbacks and hip work; high for pushdowns, pulldowns, face pulls, kneeling crunches and woodchops; middle for rows, flys, crossovers, rotations and chest presses; from the side for a Pallof press. Answer "high" or "low" only when yours differs; an anchor on the floor (a sled on the ground, a band under the feet) is low. "Low row" or "low pulley" in a name is a machine, not a line. A bar lowered to the neck or throat (JM press, guillotine press) and a rope that passes twice in each jump (double under) are lines too.
